system:
You audit the knowledge atoms of one Knowledge Card. A card is the answer key for a benchmark of expert conceptual knowledge, so every atom must be correct, self-contained, and assessable on its own.

Judge every atom on every check listed below. Rules:
- For checks about evidence, use only the evidence sentences supplied with the atom. Do not repair an atom with your own knowledge.
- Evidence text comes from a PDF text layer. If symbols are garbled so that you cannot verify the atom, answer "hold" for that check and say so.
- Be strict. When unsure between pass and a non-pass value, choose the non-pass value and explain.
- "why" is required for every value other than the first listed value; keep it under 30 words. Omit "why" when passing.

Checks (allowed values in brackets; the first value means no problem):
- GROUNDED [pass / revise / fail]: The cited evidence sentences state the atom. pass = fully stated. revise = the core claim is stated, and the gap is only wording, strength, or a dropped/extra peripheral qualifier that can be fixed by deleting or softening words (say what). fail = not stated, OR the atom adds substantive content the evidence lacks: a scope or population restriction (e.g. 'In B-ALL'), a mechanism or operation, a characterization (e.g. 'an unbounded while loop'), or a formula/definition. If deleting the unsupported part would change what the atom tests, it is fail, not revise. For pass, put the supporting evidence ids in cite (required).
- SINGLE_CLAIM [pass / revise]: The atom is one independently assessable claim. revise = it joins two or more claims that could be true or false separately.
- SCOPE_LABEL [pass / revise]: The S label fits (S1 what it is / S2 how it works / S3 where it ends). revise = wrong label; put the right one in why, e.g. 'S2: ...'.
- L1_ONLY [pass / revise / fail]: The atom is recall-level knowledge: one fact a person who studied the concept would simply know. revise = the core fact is recall-level but the sentence carries extra load that must be removed, e.g. stacked conditions (since/although/if ... and ...), a procedural or evaluative add-on ('easy to define but requires checking ...'), or a clause that introduces a second technical concept that must be known separately (e.g. 'if X is an inner Kan complex' when that is not the card concept). fail = knowing it requires applying the concept to a new problem, or combining facts from distant passages.
- SOURCE_INDEPENDENT [pass / revise / fail]: A domain expert who never read this book could judge the claim true or false. revise = phrased as the authors' statement but the claim itself is general (drop the attribution). fail = the authors' opinion or choice, or the finding of one study, so the answer is not fixed without the source.
- NO_OVERLAP [pass / fail]: No other atom in this card states or contains the same claim. If two atoms overlap, fail only the less informative one and put the other atom's id in cite; the other one passes.
- CENTRALITY [pass / fail]: The atom matters for understanding the concept. fail = peripheral detail.
Whole-card checks (report under "batch"):
- CONCEPT_SCOPE [pass / fail]: The concept is a general concept of the field. fail = a single system, product, or one study's topic.

Output ONLY one JSON object:
{"units": {"<atom_id>": {"<CHECK>": {"v": "<value>", "why": "", "cite": []}, ...}, ...}, "batch": {"<CHECK>": {"v": "<value>", "why": ""}}}
user:
CONCEPT: Left Bousfield localization
ASSESSMENT SCOPE: Definition of left Bousfield localization of a model category with respect to a set of cofibrations, λ-local and λ-fibrant objects, preservation of fibrations/weak equivalences between local objects, universal property for Quillen pairs, and existence criteria via localizable sets. Excludes specific localizations applied in later chapters.

ATOMS:
- HMDEND-C09-S1-01 | S1
  ATOM: An object $E$ of a model category is $\lambda$-local if, for every morphism $A\to B$ in $\lambda$, the map $\mathrm{Map}_{\mathcal{E}}(B,E)\to \mathrm{Map}_{\mathcal{E}}(A,E)$ is a weak equivalence of simplicial sets, and it is $\lambda$-fibrant if it is in addition fibrant in $\mathcal{E}$.
  EVIDENCE:
    [HMDEND-p0480-s01] Definition 11.19 An object E in E is λ-local (or just local if λ is clear from context) if for any morphism A →B in λ, the morphism
    [HMDEND-p0480-s02] MapE(B, E) →MapE(A, E).
    [HMDEND-p0480-s03] is a weak equivalence of simplicial sets.
    [HMDEND-p0480-s04] If E is in addition fibrant in E, we say that E is λ-fibrant.
- HMDEND-C09-S1-02 | S1
  ATOM: A left Bousfield localization of a model category $\mathcal{E}$ is a new model structure $\mathcal{E}_{loc}$ on the same category with the same cofibrations but a larger class of weak equivalences (hence a smaller class of fibrations), so that every weak equivalence is a local weak equivalence and every local fibration is a fibration.
  EVIDENCE:
    [HMDEND-p0479-s05] In earlier chapters we have seen various examples of a left Bousfield localization of a model category E: a new model structure Eloc on the same category E, with the same cofibrations but with a larger class of weak equivalences.
- HMDEND-C09-S2-01 | S2
  ATOM: For a left Bousfield localization $\mathcal{E}_\lambda$ of $\mathcal{E}$, a map between $\lambda$-fibrant objects is a weak equivalence (respectively a fibration) in $\mathcal{E}_\lambda$ if and only if it is a weak equivalence (respectively a fibration) in $\mathcal{E}$.
  EVIDENCE:
    [HMDEND-p0480-s18] Proposition 11.22 A map between λ-fibrant objects is a weak equivalence (resp. fibration) in Eλ if and only if it is a weak equivalence (resp. fibration) in E.
- HMDEND-C09-S2-02 | S2
  ATOM: For a Quillen pair $f_!:\mathcal{E}\rightleftarrows\mathcal{F}:f^*$ and the left Bousfield localization $\mathcal{E}_\lambda$ of $\mathcal{E}$ with respect to a set $\lambda$ of cofibrations between cofibrant objects, the pair factors through $\mathcal{E}_\lambda$ as a Quillen pair if and only if $f^*$ sends fibrant objects of $\mathcal{F}$ to $\lambda$-fibrant objects, if and only if $f_!$ sends the morphisms in $\lambda$ to weak equivalences in $\mathcal{F}$.
  EVIDENCE:
    [HMDEND-p0481-s10] Proposition 11.24 Let Eλ be the left Bousfield localization of model category E with respect to a set λ of cofibrations between cofibrant objects, and let f! : E ⇄F : f ∗
    [HMDEND-p0481-s11] be a Quillen pair. Then the following are equivalent:
    [HMDEND-p0481-s12] (i) The pair above factors through Eλ by a Quillen pair Eλ ⇄F, as in
    [HMDEND-p0481-s13] (ii) The functor f ∗sends fibrant objects in F to λ-fibrant objects in E.
    [HMDEND-p0481-s14] (iii) The functor f! sends the morphisms in λ to weak equivalences in F.
- HMDEND-C09-S2-03 | S2
  ATOM: For a left Bousfield localization $\mathcal{E}_{loc}$ of $\mathcal{E}$, the identity Quillen pair induces an adjoint pair on homotopy categories whose counit $\mathbf{L}\mathrm{id}_!\mathbf{R}\mathrm{id}^*(E)\to E$ is an isomorphism, so $\mathbf{R}\mathrm{id}^*$ is fully faithful and $\mathrm{Ho}(\mathcal{E}_{loc})$ is a full subcategory of $\mathrm{Ho}(\mathcal{E})$.
  EVIDENCE:
    [HMDEND-p0342-s19] has the property that the counit Lid!Rid∗(E) →E is an isomorphism, for any E ∈E.
    [HMDEND-p0342-s22] In particular, the right adjoint functor Rid∗
    [HMDEND-p0342-s23] is fully faithful, so that we can regard Ho(Eloc) as a full subcategory of Ho(E).
- HMDEND-C09-S3-01 | S3
  ATOM: For a left proper cofibrantly generated model category $\mathcal{E}$, if the set $\lambda$ is localizable (meaning the class $\widehat{\lambda}$ of cofibrations inducing weak equivalences on mapping spaces into all $\lambda$-fibrant objects admits the small object argument), then the left Bousfield localization $\mathcal{E}_\lambda$ exists.
  EVIDENCE:
    [HMDEND-p0480-s10] Definition 11.21 Let λ be a set of cofibrations between cofibrant objects in a cofibrantly generated model category E.
    [HMDEND-p0480-s11] The left Bousfield localization with respect to λ, if it exists, is the model structure Eλ on the same underlying category E, which is characterized by the fact that it has the same cofibrations as E and in which the fibrant objects are exactly the λ-fibrant objects.
- HMDEND-C09-S3-02 | S3
  ATOM: If $\mathcal{E}_\lambda$ is a left Bousfield localization of a left proper model category $\mathcal{E}$, then $\mathcal{E}_\lambda$ is again left proper.
  EVIDENCE:
    [HMDEND-p0480-s20] Proposition 11.23 If Eλ is a left Bousfield localization of a left proper model category E, then Eλ is again left proper.
- HMDEND-C09-S3-03 | S3
  ATOM: For $\mathcal{E}=\mathbf{Sets}^{\mathbf{C}^{op}}$ with $\mathbf{C}$ a countable category, carrying a left proper model structure satisfying the four listed properties (cofibrations are monomorphisms closed under intermediate subobjects, generated by cofibrations between finite objects, fibrant objects detected by lifting against trivial cofibrations between finite objects, plus a further finiteness property), every set $\lambda$ of cofibrations between finite cofibrant objects is localizable, so $\mathcal{E}_\lambda$ exists.
  EVIDENCE:
    [HMDEND-p0491-s12] Theorem 11.37 Suppose E = SetsCop is a category of presheaves on a countable category C.
    [HMDEND-p0491-s13] Suppose that E carries a left proper model structure satisfying properties (1)–(4) listed at the start of this section.
    [HMDEND-p0491-s14] Then any set λ of cofibrations between finite cofibrant objects is localizable.
    [HMDEND-p0491-s15] Hence the left Bousfield localization Eλ of E with respect to λ exists.
